D.t: David Jolly trails by 3.2 and wins 28% of simulations. Closing it takes about 145,312 voters switching sides, or 290,624 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +11.0 and D +4.9. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +4.7. Your best recent poll is Change Research at D +0.8; your worst is YouGov for N+ Univision at R +9.1. 16 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Broward, a projected net 231,784 votes; Orange, a projected net 123,019 votes; Palm Beach, a projected net 84,140 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Miami-Dade, D +0.1, 9.5% of the vote; Hillsborough, D +8.9, 6.3% of the vote; Pinellas, D +8.3, 5.1% of the vote; Duval, D +9.1, 4.4% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, David Jolly runs furthest behind in Okaloosa, Collier, Clay. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 79% of voters, 50 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.96 points; White voters, 69% of voters, 40 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.44 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 68% of voters, 47 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.38 points.

The forecast's worst groups for David Jolly: Immigration voters 15 to 83, Voters who can afford daily costs 37 to 61, Midsize counties 38 to 60. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.0M cash against $44.0M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
